words.meaning: to be able to do, to be good at
you (to someone of equal or lower status)
pardon me, excuse me (e.g. when leaving)
to persevere, to do one's best

一.components: pictograph — one horizontal stroke, one tally mark

七.components: pictograph — a horizontal stroke cut by a vertical hook
七.note: Originally the sign for 'cut' (a line being sliced); borrowed for the sound of 'seven'. Brute force — the shape has nothing to do with sevenness.

丈.components: 十 ten + a long diagonal sweep (乂)
丈.note: Originally a hand holding a measuring staff — a 丈 was a unit of height. Think: a tall measuring stick.

上.components: a mark sitting above a baseline
上.note: The long bottom stroke is the ground; the stub and vertical stick up out of it. 下 is the same idea flipped.

世.components: three joined tens (十十十) written as one shape
世.note: Thirty years = one generation = an age = the world of that age.

中.components: 口 a box/enclosure + │ a line skewered through its center
中.note: A pole planted dead-center through a frame.

九.components: pictograph — a bent arm, or a hook curling back
九.note: Traditionally an elbow bending; mostly borrowed for sound. Treat as brute force.

事.components: 一 top stroke + 口 mouth + 彐 hand + 亅 hook running through
事.note: A hand holding up a banner or writing-tablet — the ritual officer's duty. Drawing-wise the hooked vertical is one long spear down the middle; write it last.

五.components: two horizontal lines (heaven and earth) with a crossed X between them
五.note: Originally crossed counting-sticks between two boundary lines; the crossing is the only hook worth keeping.

人.components: pictograph — a person in profile, two legs walking

今.components: 亽 lid/cover over ラ-like tuck
今.note: Eroded — a cover closing over the present moment. Mostly brute force; contrast with 令 and 会, which share the same 亽 roof.

仕.note: a person serving a lord — 仕 originally meant 'to serve'; 士 is also the sound (shi)

会.note: People gathering under one roof — the bottom was originally a lid fitting a pot, i.e. two things meeting.

伝.note: person passing words along — 云 is the old form of 'say'; the modern shape is a simplification of 傳

住.note: the master of the house is the person who lives there; 主 also carries the sound (juu)

何.note: 可 is phonetic (ka). Original meaning was a person carrying a load; 'what' is a borrowing.

作.note: 乍 is phonetic (saku) — no real story in the right side, treat the shape as brute force

使.note: a person sending an official on an errand — 使 is both 'envoy' and 'use'

信.note: a person standing by their word — trust

俺.note: 奄 is purely phonetic here; the 'I' meaning is a Japanese borrowing. Brute force

僕.components: 亻 person + 業-like right side 菐
僕.note: 菐 is phonetic (boku); the character meant 'manservant' — humble 'I'. Right side has no clean story, memorize the shape: 业 over 关-ish

優.components: 亻 person + 憂 grief (百 head + 冖 cover + 心 heart + 夂 slow steps)
優.note: a person who feels another's grief-heavy heart is gentle; 憂 is also the sound (yuu)

元.note: pictograph of a person with the head emphasized on top — the head is the 'origin/beginning'

兄.note: A person with a big mouth — the older brother is the one who does the talking.

先.components: 𠂉/牛-top foot mark + 儿 legs/person
先.note: A footprint above a person's legs — the foot that went ahead. Hence 'previous, ahead'.

入.components: pictograph — a narrow opening / a person bending into an entrance
入.note: note the stroke order: short left stroke first, then the long right. Mirror-check against 人

全.note: Perfect jade kept whole under a roof — hence 'complete, entire'.

八.note: original meaning 'divide'; the number eight is a sound borrowing

六.components: 亠 lid + 八 splitting legs
六.note: shape is a pictograph of a hut; the number six is a sound borrowing — brute force

出.note: pictograph of a foot stepping out of a cave mouth — the 山s are not really mountains. Draw it as a small U inside a taller U

分.components: 八 split apart + 刀 sword
分.note: A sword cutting something into two parts — hence divide, portion, minute. 分かる = things become clear once they're separated out.

前.components: 丷 two horns + 一 line + 月 flesh/moon + 刂 knife
前.note: Historically 止 foot + boat + knife — eroded beyond recognition. Treat as brute force: horns over a line, flesh, knife on the right.

力.components: pictograph — a bent arm flexing, or a plow, depending who you ask
力.note: Two strokes, one hook. Either image works; the arm is easier to feel while writing.

勉.note: 免 is phonetic (ben), but readable: put strength into escaping — effort, diligence.

動.note: Strength applied to something heavy makes it move.

十.components: pictograph — a single vertical line later crossed to mark the full count
十.note: Brute force: the crossbar is a bookkeeping mark, not a picture of anything.

単.components: 丷 two horns + 田 field-shape + 十 stem
単.note: simplified from 單; the shape is eroded — brute force this one, no honest story left

友.components: ナ hand on top + 又 hand below
友.note: Two hands reaching toward each other — a friend.

同.components: 冂 enclosure + 一 + 口 mouth
同.note: Mouths inside one frame all saying the same thing.

名.note: In the dark of evening you can't be seen, so you speak your name aloud.

君.components: ヨ-like hand holding a staff (尹) + 口 mouth
君.note: A hand with a baton plus a mouth giving orders — originally a ruler, softened into casual 'you'.

味.note: 未 is phonetic (mi). Still, 'mouth + not yet' as taste-you-can't-quite-name is a serviceable hook.

呼.note: 口 gives the meaning, 乎 gives the sound — no story in the right side, just memorize the shape: 丿 over 一 over the 亏 hook.

四.components: 囗 enclosure + 儿-like legs inside
四.note: Brute force — the original 'four' was four horizontal strokes; this shape was borrowed for the sound. Draw it as a box with two legs kicking inward.

回.components: 口 outer enclosure + 口 inner enclosure
回.note: A spiral/whirlpool drawn as boxes inside boxes — turning, going around, hence counting 'times'.

国.note: The treasure kept inside the borders — a country.

場.components: 土 earth + 昜 sun rising over rays
場.note: A patch of ground with the sun on it — an open place. The right side is mainly phonetic; hold it as 日 + 一 + 勿.

声.components: 士 scholar-shape on top + 尸-like body below
声.note: Simplified from 聲 (a chime + hand + ear). What's left is arbitrary — brute force the shape: 士 over a flat 尸.

変.components: 亦 (top: 亠 + 小-ish legs) + 夂 trailing foot
変.note: Modern shape is a simplification of 變 (糸+言+糸 over 攴) — the top is eroded and not worth a story. Brute force the top; 夂 at the bottom is the same trailing foot as in 夏/後.

多.note: Evening stacked on evening — many nights pile up.

夜.components: 亠 lid + 亻 person (squeezed on the left) + 夕 evening + 乀 sweeping stroke
夜.note: A person out under the lid of the sky with an evening moon beside them. The final sweeping stroke is just shape — don't overthink it.

夢.components: 艹 grass + 罒 eye (sideways) + 冖 cover + 夕 evening
夢.note: Eyes covered in the evening — that's when you dream. The 艹 on top was originally eyebrows/lashes over the eye, not grass.

大.components: pictograph — a person standing with arms and legs stretched wide
大.note: The full-body stretch is the whole idea: big.

夫.components: 大 big person + 一 hairpin across the top
夫.note: A grown man with a pin through his topknot — the hairpin marks adulthood. Note it's 大 with a line above, vs 天 where the top line is the sky.

失.components: 𠂉 slanted top stroke + 大-ish body, i.e. 手 hand with something slipping out
失.note: Originally a hand (手) with a stroke marking something dropping out of it — to lose. Note it is NOT 矢 arrow: the top stroke pokes out to the left and the vertical doesn't cross the top.

女.components: pictograph — a kneeling woman with crossed arms, seen from the side

奴.note: A hand seizing a woman — originally a slave/servant, hence the derogatory tone still on 奴 today.

好.note: Mother and child side by side — the image of something good and liked.

妹.note: The woman who is not yet grown — younger sister. 未 also carries the sound (mai), so it works twice.

姉.components: 女 woman + 市-like right side
姉.note: The right side is phonetic (from 市 shi → shimai 姉妹), not a story. Contrast with 妹: 未 not-yet = younger, so 姉 is the other one.

始.note: 台 is phonetic (shi). If you want a hook: a woman is where every life begins.

姿.components: 次 next/order (冫 + 欠) on top + 女 woman below
姿.note: 次 is phonetic (shi). The 女 underneath gives the sense of figure/form/bearing.

嫌.note: 兼 is phonetic (ken). Loose hook if you need it: holding two things at once (兼) breeds resentment — but the sound is the real reason it's there.

嬉.components: 女 woman + 喜 rejoice (士 + 口 + 丷 + 口)
嬉.note: 喜 gives both sound (ki) and meaning — a drum (the top half was originally a drum on a stand) over a mouth 口 shouting for joy.

子.components: pictograph — a baby: big head (the top 了 curve), swaddled arms (the horizontal stroke), body wrapped up

学.components: ⺍ three small strokes + 冖 cover + 子 child
学.note: A child under the roof of a school, hands reaching down from above to teach. Simplified from 學, where the top was hands and a lattice.

守.note: a hand under the roof — you guard the house you're inside of

家.note: A pig under the roof — livestock lived in the house. 豕 is worth learning as a unit: it only shows up in a handful of kanji.

寝.components: 宀 roof + 爿 (narrow) bed + 侵-right (彐 hand + 又/夂 hand with broom)
寝.note: the right-bottom is eroded; treat the whole right half as 'the 侵 shape' and drill it — under a roof, on a bed

小.components: pictograph — three small specks, a hook with a dot each side

少.components: 小 small + a slash cutting across
少.note: small with a piece struck off it — even less

屋.components: 尸 corpse/flag-like roof + 至 arrive
屋.note: 尸 is the bent-body shape used for buildings/coverings — you arrive under the roof. Genuinely a decent story for once.

山.components: pictograph — three peaks rising from one baseline
山.note: Center peak tallest. Draw center stroke first, then the left hook, then the right vertical.

帰.components: 刂-like 刀 stroke + 彐 hand + 巾 cloth
帰.note: left side is a worn-down remnant, not a real component anymore; the 彐+巾 half is a hand holding cloth. Brute force the left stroke

年.components: 𠂉 sloping stroke + 手-like body over 十
年.note: Originally 禾 grain over 人 person — a man carrying the harvest home, one harvest = one year. The modern shape is squashed beyond recognition, so treat the strokes as brute force and keep the harvest image only as a memory hook.

度.components: 广 roof/lean-to + 廿 twenty (the horizontals) + 又 hand
度.note: A hand measuring spans under a shelter — measuring gives 'degree, extent, occasion'.

座.components: 广 lean-to roof + 人 person + 人 person + 土 earth
座.note: two people sitting on the ground under a shelter

弟.components: 丷 + 弓-ish body + 丿 slash
弟.note: originally cord wound in order around a stake — the ordering gave 'younger'. The modern shape is too eroded to draw that story; learn it as a whole

張.note: stretching a bow out long — one of the cleanest compounds on this list.

強.components: 弓 bow + 厶 small + 虫 insect
強.note: Right side is originally a beetle name, purely phonetic here. Hold onto 弓 bow + 虫 bug as a shape hook: a bow strong enough that the drawstring hums like an insect.

当.components: ⺌ three small strokes + ヨ hand shape
当.note: Simplified from 當 (尚 + 田) — the modern shape is arbitrary. Brute force: small strokes over a ヨ.

彼.note: 皮 is phonetic — it carries the sound, not a story. 彳 marks it as a going-over-there word: that one, over there

待.note: pairs with 時 (日+寺) and 持 (扌+寺) — same right side, swap the left

心.components: pictograph — a heart with its chambers, three dots off a curved stroke

忘.components: 亡 to perish (top) + 心 heart (bottom)
忘.note: 亡 is both sound and sense — what dies out of the heart is forgotten

忙.components: 忄 heart (side form) + 亡 perish
忙.note: 亡 is phonetic, same sound as 忘; heart on the left instead of the bottom — busy is the heart perishing

思.components: 田 field (was 囟 skull/fontanel) + 心 heart
思.note: the top was originally a skull, flattened into 田 — head over heart is thinking

悪.note: 亜 is largely phonetic, but reads well as a mnemonic: a second-rate heart is a bad heart. 心 at the bottom is the 'heart-as-base' shape, not the 忄 side form.

意.note: The sound that comes out of the heart — what you mean. Genuine old reading, and a rare case where the story matches.

感.note: 咸 is phonetic (kan). Break the top half as 厂 + 一 + 口 + 戈 halberd for drawing — the internal shape is eroded, so it's mostly brute force.

戻.note: The bottom was originally 犬 dog — a dog coming back in under the door — but modern Japanese writes plain 大. Draw 大, remember the dog.

所.note: An axe by the door — the spot where the work gets done. The pairing is largely phonetic, but the image holds up for writing.

手.components: pictograph — an open hand with fingers and wrist
手.note: The three horizontals are fingers, the vertical hook is the arm.

持.note: 寺 is phonetic (ji), same as in 時 and 侍. Hand-side + temple: you hold something.

教.components: 耂 old + 子 child + 攵 strike/action
教.note: An elder, a child, and a hand with a stick — teaching, old-style. The left half (孝 filial piety) is what you actually draw as one unit.

方.components: pictograph — a plow, or two boats lashed side by side
方.note: Genuinely disputed and eroded. Brute force the shape: 亠 lid over a hook with a sweep.

族.components: 方 banner-pole + 𠂉 flag flying + 矢 arrow
族.note: the left side 㫃 is a banner streaming from a pole; arrows gathered under one clan banner

日.components: pictograph — the sun, a circle with a mark in the middle, squared off

早.note: Sun over a stroke marking the horizon — sun just up, therefore early. The bottom isn't really 'ten', but drawing it as 十 works.

昨.note: 乍 is purely phonetic (saku). Sun for 'day' is the meaningful half; the right side is brute force — just note it's the same 乍 as in 作 minus the 亻.

時.note: 寺 is phonetic here, but the temple bell marking the hours by the sun is a clean hook.

暇.note: 叚 is phonetic (ka), same right side as 仮 and 霞. The shape is arbitrary — memorize it as a unit: 𠃍 + 二 + 又-ish. Days with sun and nothing to do.

月.components: pictograph — a crescent moon with two clouds crossing it
月.note: The two inner strokes are what keeps it from being 日. Note: as a left/bottom component in body words (胸, 服, 腹) this same shape is actually 肉 flesh, not moon.

朝.components: 十 + 日 sun + 十 on the left (草 grass sandwiching the sun) + 月 moon
朝.note: Sun rising through the grass while the moon is still up — that's morning.

本.components: 木 tree + 一 mark at the base
本.note: The stroke marks the tree's roots — the origin, the source. Book comes later via 'source text'.

束.components: 木 tree with 口 band tied around its middle
束.note: a bundle of sticks with a cord around it — 約束 is literally 'tie + bundle'

来.components: 一 top stroke + 米-like body (two 人 flanking a central stem)
来.note: Originally a pictograph of a wheat/barley plant with drooping ears — the grain that 'came' to the fields. Just draw it as a vertical stem with two pairs of arms and a crossbar.

校.note: 交 is mainly phonetic (kou), though 'where people mix' is a usable hook for school.

楽.components: 白 white + two 幺 threads flanking + 木 tree
楽.note: Originally a picture of a wooden instrument with strings — music, hence pleasure. Draw it as: small horns, then 白, then 木.

様.components: 木 tree + 羊 sheep + 永-bottom (water tail)
様.note: The right side 羕 is phonetic (yō). Practical drawing order: 木, then 羊 on top right, then the three-stroke 'flowing water' tail underneath.

次.components: 冫 two strokes + 欠 lack/yawn
次.note: 欠 is a person with mouth open. Left side is two strokes, not really 'ice' here — the origin is eroded; treat it as brute force.

止.components: pictograph — a footprint (toes and heel) planted on the ground
止.note: A foot that has stopped. It's the ancestor of the 'foot' element in 歩 and 走.

死.components: 歹 bare bones + 匕 kneeling person
死.note: A person crouched beside stripped bones — the original picture of mourning the dead. 歹 is a cracked skeleton fragment.

母.components: pictograph — 女 woman with two dots added for breasts
母.note: Draw it as 女 rewritten with the two dots in the middle: a woman who is nursing.

毎.components: 𠂉 slanted top stroke + 母 mother
毎.note: 母 with a hat on. Sound-wise related to 母; treat the top as just a lid you always draw before the mother.

気.components: 气 rising vapor + 〆 (simplified from 米 rice)
気.note: steam rising off cooking rice — energy, spirit

水.components: pictograph — a central current with spray flying off both sides
水.note: The middle vertical is the stream; the four side strokes are splashing water. Squashed to 氵 on the left of other kanji.

沢.note: 尺 is phonetic here — no story in it. Meaning is 'marsh/swamp', water spread wide, which is why 沢山 means 'a heap of'.

無.components: top pile of strokes (一 + 卌-like uprights) + 灬 fire below
無.note: Originally a person dancing with sleeves/plumes (the ancestor of 舞), borrowed purely for the sound meaning 'not have'. The meaning is a loan — no story connects the shape to 'nonexistent'. Mnemonic if you want one: everything burned in the fire, so there is nothing left.

然.components: 月 meat + 犬 dog + 灬 fire
然.note: Literally dog meat over a fire — originally 'to burn'. The modern 'thus, so' sense is a borrowing, so treat the meaning link as brute force; the picture is just for recall.

父.components: pictograph — a hand gripping a stone axe
父.note: The two upper strokes are the hand, the crossing 乂 is the axe. The one who swings the tool.

物.components: 牛 cow (squashed to 牜) + 勿 banner streamers
物.note: 勿 is mostly phonetic. The cow side is real though — livestock was the archetypal 'thing you own', so 物 = stuff.

理.components: 王 jade (not king) + 里 village
理.note: On the left this is 玉 jade with the dot dropped. The original sense is the veins running through a piece of jade — cut along the grain and it splits clean; that grain became 'logic, reason'. 里 is phonetic.

生.note: A plant pushing up out of the earth — life, birth, growth.

申.components: 田 field with a vertical stroke driven through it
申.note: Originally a lightning bolt zigzagging down — the sky speaking. Hence 'to say (humbly)'. The 田 is not a field, just the bolt's kinked middle.

男.note: Strength in the rice field. One of the cleanest, most literal compounds in the whole set.

町.note: 丁 is a nail seen from the side, and mostly phonetic here. Fields divided into blocks — a settled, gridded place: town.

界.components: 田 field + 介 to come between
界.note: 介 is a person 人 with something on either side — the thing wedged between fields is the boundary.

番.components: 釆 scattered rice/claw-marks on top + 田 field
番.note: Originally an animal's paw-print pressed into a field — tracks come one after another, hence 'turn, in sequence, number'.

白.components: 丿 stroke on top of 日 sun
白.note: A ray coming off the sun = bright = white. (Origin is contested — possibly an acorn or a thumbnail — but the sunbeam image is the practical one.)

目.note: Originally horizontal with a pupil inside; rotated 90° when writing went vertical. The two inner strokes are the iris.

相.note: an eye looking at a tree — two things facing each other, hence 'mutual' and 相手 'the one facing you'

知.note: words fly from the mouth straight as an arrow — you say it fast because you know it

礼.note: 礻 is the altar radical (from 示) — anything to do with gods, ritual, ceremony. The right side is a simplification of 豊 in 禮; the hook itself is arbitrary.

私.components: 禾 grain stalk + 厶 private/self
私.note: 厶 was originally the pictograph for 'private, cocooning one's own arm around something'. Grain you enclose for yourself = mine = I.

立.components: pictograph — a person standing with arms out on the ground line at the bottom

笑.note: bamboo bending in the wind like a body doubled over laughing; 夭 alone is a person with head tilted

簡.components: ⺮ bamboo + 間 interval (門 gate + 日 sun)
簡.note: bamboo writing-strips — the simple note; 間 is mostly phonetic here

約.note: tying a thread around something to bind it — 勺 is phonetic

続.note: 売 is phonetic here — it carries the sound, not a story

置.components: 罒 net on top + 直 straight/fix
置.note: Net cast down and set straight — you place it there.

考.components: 耂 old man (top of 老) + 丂 hook
考.note: an old man bent over — long thought; 丂 is phonetic

聞.note: an ear at the gate, listening to what's on the other side

自.components: pictograph — a nose seen from the front
自.note: Japanese speakers point at their own nose to mean 'me'

葉.components: 艹 grass + 世 generation + 木 tree
葉.note: leaves on a tree, generation after generation; 世 also carries the sound

行.components: 彳 left step + 亍 right step
行.note: Originally a pictograph of a crossroads. Two feet stepping into an intersection = go.

見.note: An eye walking on legs — a person looking.

解.components: 角 horn + 刀 knife + 牛 cow
解.note: Knife taking the horn off an ox — butchering, taking apart. That's literally 'to disassemble', and by extension to solve or understand.

言.components: 亠 + 二 stacked lines + 口 mouth
言.note: Lines of sound rising out of a mouth.

許.note: words that grant permission — 午 is purely phonetic, no story in it

訳.note: 尺 is phonetic (same right side as 沢, 択). Words measured over into another language: translation, and hence 'the reason/excuse behind the words' in 申し訳ない.

話.note: 舌 is itself 千 + 口, a tongue sticking out of a mouth. Speech plus tongue = talk. (舌 is doing phonetic duty too, but the tongue image is honest.)

語.components: 訁 words + 五 five + 口 mouth
語.note: The right side 吾 is phonetic (go), but five mouths talking is a fair hook for language.

誰.components: 訁 words + 隹 short-tailed bird
誰.note: 隹 is phonetic; 'who' is an abstract word with no picture behind it — brute force

調.components: 訁 words + 周 circumference/all around
調.note: words sent all around to check on things — 周 also carries the sound. Fine as a hook, but the sound link is the load-bearing part.

買.components: 罒 net (on its side) + 貝 shell/money
買.note: net over money — you scoop up goods with cash. 罒 here is a net, not an eye.

進.components: 隹 small bird + 辶 movement road
進.note: a bird moving along the road — birds hop forward, never backward.

達.components: 辶 road + 幸 (looks like 土 earth over 羊-ish body) + 寸-less right side
達.note: Practically: 辶 road + 幸 luck-shape. The right side is phonetic and eroded — draw 土 then the 羊-like body, and don't hunt for a story.

違.components: 韋 tanned leather/opposing feet + 辶 movement road
違.note: 韋 is two feet pointing away from each other — going different ways on the road. Mostly phonetic, but the two-feet shape is real.

選.components: 巳 + 巳 two kneeling people + 共 together + 辶 movement road
選.note: top half is 巽 — two people presented together; you pick from the pair and send them down the road. The 巳巳 shapes are eroded, just drill the twin tops.

部.components: 立 stand + 口 mouth (together = 咅) + 阝 village (right side)
部.note: 阝 on the right is village/city; on the left it's hill. 咅 is purely phonetic here — brute force the left half.

配.components: 酉 wine jar + 己 kneeling person
配.note: someone crouched beside the wine jar, portioning it out — distribute

間.note: Sunlight through the crack between the gate doors — the gap, the interval.

難.components: 廿 + 口 + 夫 (left stack) + 隹 small bird
難.note: left side is eroded beyond rescue — treat it as a fixed three-part stack you drill. Only 隹 bird is trustworthy. This one is brute force.

面.components: 一 top + 囬 enclosed frame around a shape
面.note: Pictograph of a face inside a mask/outline — the 目-like box is the eye in the face. Mostly brute force to write; drill the outer box order.

頑.note: 元 is phonetic (gan). 頁 is the big head/face element — it means head, not page, in kanji. Stubborn head, if you want a hook.

頭.note: 豆 is phonetic (tou), but a bean on top of the 頁 head-element is a fine drawing hook.

頼.components: 束 bundle + 刀-ish stroke + 頁 head
頼.note: left side is 剌 squashed; treat 束 + the short right strokes as one memorized unit. The 頁 head is the only reliable half.

顔.components: 文 script/pattern + 彡 hair-strokes (together = 彦) + 頁 head
顔.note: 彦 = decorated, patterned man; 彡 is the three-stroke 'shine/hair' mark. Patterned head = face.

願.note: 原 is phonetic (gan), but the image works: you bow your head (頁) at the source of a spring (原) to make a wish.

食.components: 亽 lid/roof + 良-like body below
食.note: Pictograph of a covered bowl of food on a stand. Lift the lid and eat.

飯.components: 飠 food (eat) + 反 anti/turn over
飯.note: 反 is phonetic here (han) — no story in it; just remember the food radical on the left is a lidded bowl of grain on a stand.

飲.components: 飠 food + 欠 lack/open mouth
飲.note: 欠 is a person with mouth wide open — food side plus gaping mouth = drinking.

高.components: pictograph — a tall watchtower: roof, upper storey, lower storey
高.note: draw it as two stacked levels under a lid; that's literally the tower it came from.
